blind_flags: Tests the contested 'one of the few X who have/has' construction. Prescriptively the relative clause modifies the plural 'biologists', so 'have' is correct, but 'has' is very common in edited prose and is defended by some usage guides; the official SAT generally avoids testing this disputed point. Consider rewriting so the antecedent is unambiguous (e.g., 'Dr. Osei, unlike most marine biologists, ______ observed...').
results.blind_notes: Antecedent of 'who' is 'marine biologists' (plural), so 'have'. Most quick solvers will pick 'has' to agree with Dr. Osei. 'Having' and 'is having' create no finite verb / wrong aspect.
blind2_flags: Ambiguous key risk: in 'one of the few marine biologists who ___ observed', the antecedent of 'who' is the plural 'biologists' (she is one of the biologists who have observed...), so traditional/prescriptive grammar requires 'have' (A). If the key is 'has' (B), it is defensible only under informal notional agreement and is contestable; either way both A and B have supporters, so the item does not have exactly one uncontroversially correct answer. Recommend rewriting (e.g., 'Dr. Osei, a marine biologist, ___ observed' or remove 'one of the few').
